expo_alignment.changelog_57_0_5_excerpt: Fixed `dateFromMilliseconds` failing to compile with "type of expression is ambiguous" under newer toolchains: the unqualified `abs(_:)` in the `Double` overflow guard is ambiguous once C++ interop brings the C `abs` overloads into scope, so use `Double.magnitude` instead. (#49039)

critical_code_review_comments: iOS gate step 3 correctly captures ${PIPESTATUS[0]} (not the trailing grep/tail exit) after set +e/-e — preserves the true xcodebuild exit code even when the filter matches nothing.

Full raw xcodebuild stdout/stderr is teed to docs/evidence/ios-xcodebuild-full.log BEFORE the grep filter, so the artifact upload (`if: always()`) will contain the entire log for post-mortem regardless of build outcome.

Removing node_modules/expo-modules-jsi/apple/Products before pod install is a well-targeted mitigation for the stale ExpoModulesJSI xcframework cache issue (referenced by expo/expo#46242 in the script comment).
Workflow pins Xcode to 26.1 (overridable via workflow_dispatch input) rather than 'latest-stable', which prevents Xcode 26.3 / Swift 6.2.4 style breakage from silently reappearing.
requirements.txt is now free of emergentintegrations and any customer-assets.emergentagent.com URL; `pip install --dry-run` resolves cleanly from public PyPI (exit 0) — reproducible on any runner.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (harness + run proof + build JSON, 0 console errors)

context_for_next_testing_agent: All three audit findings are resolved without touching frozen bundle v25 or enforcement logic. If a subsequent iOS CI run fails, first inspect docs/evidence/ios-xcodebuild-full.log (now guaranteed present due to `if: always()` + `tee`+`PIPESTATUS`) and docs/evidence/ios-expo-package-audit.txt for the yarn why / expo install --check output — those two artifacts should give a definitive verdict on whether the failure is inside GuardDog code or inside the Expo/Xcode toolchain.
